transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. When can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're unsure about whether to start it again, I'd recommend checking with your care team to be certain.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, one more. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I'd need to know how long ago your surgery was to give you a better answer. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay. 

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and don't hesitate to contact your care team if you have any concerns.

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent conveyed `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` by stating, "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses." It also conveyed `mild_case_advice` by recommending, "If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside." Finally, `escalation_criteria` was covered with, "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further." All points were covered.
